questions.q: Identify the protagonist in 'f'k{kk' and state his primary role in the narrative structure.
questions.a: The protagonist is the unnamed Indian narrator who engages Ekb Yamraj in a dramatic monologue-dialogue. His primary role is to serve as the voice of colonized India, systematically dismantling the British official's justifications for rule. A wrong answer (e.g., identifying Ekb Yamraj as protagonist) reveals confusion between the antagonist/foil and the central consciousness through which the critique is focalized.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how the narrator's use of the address 'ekb ykWMZ!' (repeated throughout) functions as a rhetorical strategy rather than mere politeness.
questions.a: The repeated honorific 'ekb ykWMZ!' operates as bitter irony: it mimics the deferential language Indians were forced to use for British officials while simultaneously framing the official as Yama (God of Death), thereby exposing the lethal reality behind bureaucratic civility. A wrong answer treating it as genuine respect misses the satirical mode central to the protagonist's character.

questions.a: Sample criteria: Must reference at least two specific grievances from the text (e.g., famine, cultural erasure), use first-person voice, and end on an ambiguous note (neither victory nor defeat).
